title: Provable Benefit of SignGD: A Minimal Model Under Heavy-Tailed Class Imbalance
abstract: arXiv:2512.00763v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Adaptive and non-Euclidean optimizers often outperform Euclidean methods such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD) in language modeling by a large margin. Existing theory usually explains this gap by assuming favorable smoothness geometry or noise structure tailored to the specific optimizer. We instead ask whether such geometry can be induced from a concrete learning setting. Starting from an optimizer gap that persists across realistic language-modeling experiments, we progressively remove sequence dependence, architectural complexity, and stochasticity. We find that the gap exists in a minimal setting: the softmax unigram model with heavy-tailed data. This model exposes a simple deterministic mechanism under heavy-tailed class imbalance. We prove that GD learns rare tokens slowly because the corresponding logits receive only tiny updates, while SignGD removes this magnitude dependence and moves rare and common coordinates on

translated_title: SignGD的可证明优势：重尾类别不平衡下的极简模型
translated_abstract: 自适应和非欧几里得优化器在语言建模中往往大幅优于随机梯度下降（SGD）等欧几里得方法。现有理论通常通过假设针对特定优化器量身定制的有利光滑性几何结构或噪声结构来解释这一差距。我们转而探究这种几何结构是否可以从具体的学习环境中自然产生。从在现实语言建模实验中持续存在的优化器差距出发，我们逐步去除序列依赖性、架构复杂性和随机性。我们发现这一差距存在于一个极简设置中：具有重尾数据的softmax一元语法（unigram）模型。该模型揭示了重尾类别不平衡下一个简单的确定性机制。我们证明GD学习稀有token很慢，因为相应的logits只能收到微小的更新，而SignGD消除了这种幅值依赖，使稀有token和常见token的坐标在同等程度上移动……
tldr: 该论文证明在重尾类别不平衡的极简softmax unigram模型中，SignGD因消除了梯度幅值依赖而能比GD更快地学习稀有token，从而解释了自适应优化器在语言建模中优于SGD的差距。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that in a minimal softmax unigram model under heavy-tailed class imbalance, SignGD learns rare tokens faster than GD by removing gradient-magnitude dependence, explaining the optimizer gap between adaptive methods and SGD in language modeling.
